Our kids will have to work smarter, not just harder. As Al takes over technical tasks, human “power skills” become more valuable, and we need to shift our focus to equipping kids with these skills. 

The truth is that our education system is still teaching kids to master Monopoly... while the real world is playing 4D chess against robots.

Remember when
“study hard → get degree
→ work same job for 40 years → retire with a gold watch” was the master plan?
That’s no longer relevant advice. 

I recommend parents & schools start prioritizing these 4 skills:

💥1. Adaptability/Agency (AKA thriving in chaos) 

The ability to pivot  with swift, nimble, and proactive thinking will be the defining skill of the post-AI era. There is no space for victim mentalities; only action and agency. Agency is not delusional optimism, but an unshakeable sense of confidence. The world could be spinning, job markets failing, careers tanking, but those with agency will come out on top.

💥Creative Problem-Solving

A new paper came out examining 50 years of research. According to the findings, the equation is simple: mastery of knowledge + the real-world application of knowledge = a creative problem-solver. 

💥Self-Driven Learning

“Self-directed learning” happens when the student takes full ownership of their educational journey: setting goals, managing time, reflecting on their progress, pursuing excellence, and so on. In a nutshell, self-directed learning is the desire to grow and the belief that we will never stop growing. This is one of our core beliefs: kids are limitless. Limitless environments require space for kids to fail, but most importantly, space to fail safely.

💥Emotional Intelligence 

AI may automate entire jobs and swallow entire industries, but it will lack the ability to deeply understand humans. Motivations, emotions, and human tendencies will become even more important to understand. Which means that human-to-human skills will become more valuable, not less. Negotiation. Persuasion. Storytelling. Leadership. These are not soft skills. They are power skills.
